items.title: Connecting artificial intelligence with the tools of astrophysical research
items.excerpt: AstroGenesis (ICRANet-Armenia, arXiv) is a multi-agent AI for astrophysics: a supervisor coordinates agents that search literature, pull observational data and run physics models, while neural emulators trained on model outputs speed parameter exploration.

items.title: Twisted atomic layers slide spontaneously at room temperature in simulations
items.excerpt: Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers used a high-accuracy machine-learning interatomic potential to simulate >10,000-atom twisted bilayer MoS2, finding defect-free layers slide at ~1 m/s at room temperature while ~0.1% sulfur vacancies pin them (JACS).

items.title: Predicting jumping genes' roles in changing genome size
items.excerpt: Ohio State's PrinTE forward simulator uses machine learning to steer millions of generations of transposable-element insertions and deletions toward plausible evolutionary histories; in myrtle rust, insertions outpaced deletions 4-5x (Nature Communications).

items.title: SYNAPS-I: Intelligent computing transforms X-ray imaging, from data collection to discovery
items.excerpt: DOE SYNAPS-I (Berkeley Lab ALS, Brookhaven NSLS-II, Argonne): ML lets an X-ray microscope pick regions autonomously, a foundation model reconstructs ptychography at 200 images/s, and a 3D chip was rebuilt from ~1/10 the usual data with a fine-tuned SAM 3.

items.title: Let there be light—novel AI framework runs on optical hardware
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo and NTT combine an SS-DFA training method with a single-map network to cut measurement and compute for physics-based AI; on an optical computing system it matched or beat more complex networks (Nature Computational Science).

items.title: Chatbots with personality? How AI describes itself and judges us
items.excerpt: JGU Mainz compared self-descriptions from seven language models with 70 humans: models portrayed themselves as more conscientious, agreeable and stable, and humans spotted AI vs human texts better (83%) than chatbots did (67%) (Scientific Reports).

items.title: Prior expertise may determine whether AI builds skills or substitutes for them, field experiment suggests
items.excerpt: A field experiment with patent lawyers suggests that whether on-the-job AI builds expertise or erodes it depends on how much expertise people bring to the tool in the first place.

items.title: One of AI's most annoying writing habits has a 2,000-year-old history
items.excerpt: An arXiv preprint measures how often Claude models use the 'not X, but Y' self-correction pattern versus human writing across seven genres, traces it to classical rhetoric, and pilots LoRA, prompt and sampling fixes to reduce it.

items.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers used AI to identify BRP, a natural peptide that cut food intake by up to 50% and promoted fat loss in animals via a different brain pathway than GLP-1 drugs, without the usual digestive side effects or major muscle loss.

items.title: Bird Flu Vaccine Developed Using AI Outperforms Current Stockpiled Vaccines in Preclinical Tests
items.excerpt: An AI-assisted computationally designed broad H5 vaccine antigen, DVX-panH5Nx, outperformed government-stockpiled bird flu vaccines in preclinical studies.

items.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
items.excerpt: MIT's Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins received the Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for deep-learning antibiotic discovery, including halicin and new structural classes against resistant bacteria.

items.title: Teaching AI to build better enzymes
items.excerpt: UCSB (Yang Yang) and Georgia Tech (Yunan Luo) built SynFit, an open-source ML tool that learns from several enzyme measurements at once; it guided cytochrome c variants for carbon-boron bond formation with high yield and selectivity and beat single-trait models with small datasets.

items.title: Using ChatGPT at work? Your boss may trust you less, new study finds
items.excerpt: Six studies in The Leadership Quarterly find supervisors trust employees who use LLMs less, lowering performance ratings and promotion suitability, though the penalty shrinks when organizations explicitly encourage AI use.

items.title: Machine learning decodes biochar's reactive radicals from elemental composition
items.excerpt: Kunming University of Science & Technology trained ML models on 263 records to predict biochar radical concentration and g-factor from elemental composition (shallow NN, test R2 ~0.78/0.76), partly confirmed with lab-made biochars.

items.title: Explainable AI predicts how plant compounds may cross intestinal barriers
items.excerpt: Sejong University and KIST built explainable ML models that predict intestinal permeability and efflux of plant compounds from molecular structure alone, with SHAP tying predictions to electronic, topological and branching features (J. Sci. Food Agric.).
